text:
sam: Heads-up: we need to pick a path for delegation tokens for async pipelines. Current API keys are project-scoped and used everywhere.
tay: Key pain is least-privilege: project keys used by workers widen blast radius. We should consider short-lived tokens with audience + origin claims.
leila: Agree. But rolling out new token format will hit dozens of connectors in short order. Migration complexity is real.
mike: Can we design tokens so old clients still work for a transition window? e.g. a compat flag in the auth service that accepts project keys but emits a warning and telemetry tag.
sam: Thought: token shape v1 = {iss, sub, aud, exp, route, key_id, nonce}. Nonce for replay-protection in async retries.
tay: Nonce helpful but increases state: either keep short TTL + opaque store or use sequence numbers signed into token. Which is cheaper?
leila: Prefer stateless: put a monotonic message id in token claim signed by issuer. Workers must echo it back for correlation. But reordering/retries break monotonic assumptions.
mike: Then fallback: accept nonce-less tokens but require orig_key header for lineage. Not ideal, but reduces DB load.
eng-bot: Note: any change to token claims needs update to console parsers, billing, and alert rules. See #observability for checklist.
sam: Migration plan sketch: phase 1: issue tokens for inbound webhooks only, opt-in via header X-Enable-Delegation; phase 2: default for new routes; phase 3: cutover with compat grace period where project keys work but flagged.
tay: We should also define policy for token minting. Who can mint? connectors should call auth-broker with audience+route and we check quotas + purpose. Avoid allowing public endpoints to mint.
leila: Also consider delegation chaining: connector -> worker -> sub-worker. Limit chain depth via a hop count claim. Hop=1 for workers only.
mike: RBAC: tokens should include a consumer_id claim to map to billing/owner. Could be optional for legacy keys. Add claim version so parsers know what to expect.
sam: Ops: implement TTL store for revocation list (rare, for compromise). Token introspection endpoint for on-demand validation (used by gateway). Cache introspection results at edge.
tay: Perf caveat: introspection on every request will add latency. Encourage local verification via signed JWTs with public keys rotation. Use introspection only for revoked tokens.
leila: Security: require aud=service when token used for internal RPCs. Reject tokens with mismatch. Also require presence of origin_key_id for billing reconciliation.
mike: Edge case: retries processed by different worker in other region. Must carry orig_route and orig_key to stitch logs. Prefer passing X-Origin-Route header alongside token.
eng-bot: Reminder: update the feature-flagging matrix before rollout and schedule a migration-runbook with SRE oncall.
sam: Next steps: 1) spec token v1 claims + versioning 2) prototype mint endpoint + public key rotation 3) draft migration runbook + telemetry mapping 4) spike introspection cache.
tay: I'll draft the token spec.
leila: I'll enumerate connectors likely to break and propose integration tests.
mike: I'll update observability + billing hooks.
sam: OK meet Thu 9am to review the spec. Thanks.
